citation: Jiao et al. 2023, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 67:e00197-23
design: population PK in bloodstream- and lung-infected C3HeB/FeJ mice, SC
notes: Terminal half-lives are reported in the Results: 3.39 h (bloodstream) and 4.22 h (lung) in the dose-range study 1; the abstract states about 4 h. A 35.8 h value from a moribund-mouse study is excluded. Follow-up to the 1.4 h rat value of Abdelraouf 2012; different species (mouse vs rat) and route (SC in infected mice vs IV in healthy rats).

citation: Abdelraouf et al. 2012, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 56:5724-5727
design: Single-dose IV PK of polymyxin B sulfate 4 mg/kg in 8 cannulated female Sprague-Dawley rats with component-specific serum UPLC-MS/MS; separate 3-rat self-controlled uranyl-nitrate renal-insufficiency repeat PK.
full_text_access: full (PMC full text opened with web_fetch; Europe PMC metadata/abstract opened; publisher landing page returned 403)
notes: PMC full text was accessible and paged with web_fetch; Europe PMC supplied metadata/PMCID, while the publisher landing page returned 403 in web_fetch. No supplement link was identified. All reported in-vivo PMB half-lives were serum values; no overall total-polymyxin-B serum half-life was reported. PB2 and PB3 were reported only as a combined component because the peaks were not completely resolved.

citation: Sivanesan et al. 2017, J Nat Prod 80:225-229
design: Single-dose IV rat PK: polymyxin B1, polymyxin B2, colistin A, and colistin B each dosed at 0.8 mg/kg; plasma and urine measured by LC-MS/MS, plasma protein binding by ultracentrifugation, and total/unbound PK estimated by noncompartmental analysis.
full_text_access: full (PDF supplied by the authors of this study)
notes: Table 1 gives noncompartmental elimination half-lives of 79.5, 94.9, 82.0 and 91.3 min for polymyxin B1, B2, colistin A and colistin B (n = 4 each).

design: Single-cohort serial PK application in 8 jugular-cannulated male rats given 15 mg/kg IV colistin sulfate; plasma assayed by LC-MS/MS and PK estimated by non-compartmental analysis.
full_text_access: full (publisher full text opened from Nature HTML; web_fetch used on an r.jina.ai mirror because direct Nature web_fetch returned 406)
notes: Only one in-vivo plasma half-life from the study itself was found: total colistin in rat plasma after direct IV colistin sulfate dosing (not CMS). The exact dose (15 mg/kg) is visible in Fig. 8 and reiterated in the Discussion, but the main Methods section does not clearly state the dose or full sampling-time schedule. The PK application is much more lightly reported than the assay validation. A notable internal inconsistency is the Discussion sentence attributing variability to 'conversion of the prodrug to colistin in vivo' even though the study says rats received intravenous colistin sulfate.

citation: Wang et al. 2023, J Pharm Biomed Anal 233:115440
design: Assay-validation paper with a rat colistin sulfate PK application: single intraperitoneal 3.95 mg/kg colistin sulfate in 6 male Sprague-Dawley rats, plasma sampled 0.083-24 h by UPLC-MS/MS, noncompartmental analysis of each rat (WinNonlin 5.2.1); a separate renal-accumulation study dosed 2.9 mg/kg twice daily for 1-7 days.
notes: Full text read. PK dose 3.95 mg/kg IP (Section 2.6; Table 6, n = 6); t1/2 2.53 +/- 1.6 h and MRT0-t 4.07 +/- 1.13 h. The 2.9 mg/kg q12h (5.8 mg/kg/day) dosing belongs to the kidney-accumulation groups (n = 6 each), not to the PK study. Kidney data are concentrations, not half-lives, so no kidney half-life row was added.

citation: Yapa et al. 2013, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 57:5087-5095
design: population PK of CMS and colistin, IV and intratracheal, male Sprague-Dawley rats (IV colistin sulfate 0.21, 0.41 and 0.62 mg/kg, n = 3 per dose, plasma to 4 h; three-compartment model fitted in S-ADAPT)
notes: Table 1 reports clearances and volumes but no half-life. The terminal half-life used (2.99 h) is derived by us as the slowest eigenvalue of the published three-compartment colistin model; ln2 x Vc/CL (0.49 h) is the central-volume value, kept out of the comparison. Only the colistin-sulfate dose is used; the CMS prodrug rows are not.

citation: He et al. 2013, Int J Antimicrob Agents 42:559-564
design: Single-dose IV serum/ELF PK of a polymyxin B liposome and of polymyxin B aqueous solution (USP) at about 3 mg/kg in two groups of 24 uninfected female Swiss Webster mice (4 per terminal timepoint at 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 6 h); efficacy of the liposome tested in a neutropenic murine pneumonia model.
notes: Only the aqueous-solution (USP) arm is used: it is the unformulated drug, whereas the liposome arm is a different formulation with slower clearance (reported t1/2 0.30-0.60 h). Only component-specific serum half-lives are reported (Table 1, one-compartment model).

citation: van der Meijden et al. 2023, J Antimicrob Chemother 78:832-839
design: Single-dose SC PK of polymyxin B (0.5-64 mg/kg; two mice per timepoint, 10 timepoints per dose level) in neutropenic thigh- and lung-infected female CD-1 mice, analysed with a one-compartment population PK model.
notes: No half-life is reported. It is derived by us as ln2 x Vc/F / (CL/F) from Table 1 (Vc/F 0.774 L/kg, CL/F 0.384 L/h/kg at the 10 mg/kg reference dose). Clearance falls with dose (power -0.26), so the value is dose-dependent.
half_life_method: derived: population PK, ln2 x V/CL

citation: Landersdorfer et al. 2018, J Antimicrob Chemother 73:462-468
design: Single SC doses of polymyxin B (2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 mg/kg) in neutropenic thigh-infected mice (n = 3 or 4 per time point), analysed with a two-compartment population PK model with saturable absorption and elimination.
notes: No half-life is reported and the Methods section was not in the accessible full text. The terminal half-life is derived by us from Table 1 as the slow eigenvalue of the two-compartment model at low (non-saturated) concentration: CL = linear 0.178 + Vmax/Km (0.255/0.823) L/h/kg, V1 0.325 and V2 0.808 L/kg, Q 0.198 L/h/kg.

citation: Manchandani et al. 2016, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 60:6980-6982
design: Comparative PK of the polymyxin B components after a single 3 mg/kg IV dose (10 min) in 17 female Sprague-Dawley rats, with two patients for comparison; serum sampled at 1-7.5 h and fitted to mean concentrations (one-compartment, zero-order input).
notes: Table 1: total polymyxin B t1/2 2.47 h in rats (components 2.21-3.76 h). Different paper from Manchandani2016 (biodistribution, PMID 26643340).

citation: Li et al. 2003, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 47:1766-1770

notes: Table 1: colistin t1/2 74.6 min (A 77.1, B 77.4). Clearance 5.2 mL/min/kg is nearly twice that of Sivanesan 2017 for the same species.

citation: Lin et al. 2017, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 61:e00211-17
design: population PK (two-compartment, unbound polymyxin B) in neutropenic lung-infected mice after pulmonary (4.12 and 8.24 mg base/kg) and IV (4.12 mg base/kg) dosing; plasma and ELF
notes: The paper reports t1/2 0.60 h calculated as ln2 x Vc/CL (central volume only). The value used (1.03 h) is derived by us as the slow eigenvalue of its two-compartment model (Vc 3.06, Vp 1.56 L/kg, CL 3.54, CLd 3.51 L/h/kg); the 0.60 h value is kept out of the comparison.

citation: Lin et al. 2017, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 61:e00973-17
design: population PK (two-compartment) of colistin in healthy Sprague-Dawley rats after dry-powder intratracheal (0.66 and 1.32 mg base/kg) and IV (0.66 mg base/kg) dosing; plasma and ELF
notes: No half-life is reported. The value used (10.3 h) is derived by us as the slow eigenvalue of the published model (Vc 0.572, Vp 1.47 L/kg, CL 0.271, CLd 0.172 L/h/kg); plasma was sampled to 24 h (n = 3, serial) but the slow phase is weakly determined (standard errors 35% on Vp and 24% on CLd); ln2 x Vc/CL is 1.46 h.

design: Single-dose IV PK in male Sprague-Dawley rats (carotid-cannulated; 6 rats in two groups): free colistin or colistin-loaded chelating complex micelles (CCM-CL) at 3 mg/kg infused over 15 min; plasma at 0, 15, 60, 120 and 180 min by LC-MS; free colistin fitted with a one-compartment model (PKsolver). C57BL/6 mice were used for the dose-safety and survival experiments only, not for PK.
notes: Cited as a mouse study in the request that added it; the PK arm is RAT. Free colistin t1/2 12.46 min is shorter than the 15-min infusion and rests on 3 rats and 5 samples; CCM-CL (102.23 min) is a formulation and excluded. Text says the experiments were repeated three times, so n may be larger than 3.

citation: Jin et al. 2009, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 53:4247-51
design: Single 5 mg/kg IV colistin sulfate bolus (tail vein) in 16 healthy male Swiss Outbred mice; plasma and brain at 5, 30, 60 and 120 min (n = 4 per time point, destructive sampling); HPLC with fluorescence detection
notes: Brain-penetration paper; reports plasma concentrations (Figure 2) but NO half-life. The value used is derived by us from the plotted means (read from the figure by eye), so it is approximate; 4 time points, terminal window 30-120 min.
half_life_method: derived: log-linear fit to the last 3 plotted plasma means (30-120 min), Figure 2
